title: Natural strict point map and two Roos comparison constructions
statement: Fix the finite-field datum D, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with integer ring $\mathcal O_E$, as in [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. For the actual canonical towers and augmentation of [lem-trf-point-transport-cone-comparison-descent], the level maps of [lem-trf-point-transport-strict-quotient] assemble into a natural strict tower transformation U on all complexes, whose n-th component is exactly strictQuotientPointMap. The existing actual quotient augmentation assembles into a natural transformation alpha from exact sections to the source Roos functor. The product-preserving sectionwise comparison of [lem-trf-point-quotient-augmentation-diagram], whiskered by the pullback tower, gives a natural isomorphism beta from sections of the sheaf-level pullback Roos complex to the evaluated target Roos complex. No completeness assumption is used to construct these maps.

source.place: clause *(3)*: the integral point transport is the derived limit of the levelwise maps, via its specified cone map; implementation module PointTransportTowerRealizationConstruction

proof.text: Use NatTrans.ofOpSequence on the strict finite quotient maps. The transition and arbitrary-chain-map laws give its compatibility and naturality; its component equation is definitional.

For augmentation naturality use extensionality of both Roos coordinates. The first coordinate is naturality of unrestrictedTowerUnit after exact sections; both shifted coordinates vanish. Set alpha to this natural family.
Exact point sections preserve countable products. Whisker the sectionwise normalized Roos isomorphism by the actual pullback tower to define beta.

proof_origin.place: clause *(3)*: the integral point transport is the derived limit of the levelwise maps, via its specified cone map; implementation module PointTransportTowerRealizationConstruction

mathlib_searches.query: exact evaluation of inverse towers commutes with the two-coordinate Roos mapping cocone, natural quotient augmentation, and finite Frobenius point transport
mathlib_searches.results: Generic limits and cocone comparison equations, tensor quotient maps, and inverse Frobenius on perfect rings; no coefficient-sheaf point construction. Existing project constructions are reused.
Mathlib.Algebra.Homology.HomotopyCategory.MappingCocone: mappingCocone, fst, snd, liftCochain and projection equations. These are the generic ingredients, not the specified integral point data.
Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Functor.OfSequence supplies ofOpSequence and NatTrans.ofOpSequence. No specialized realization or finite point iterate; source constructions already exist in Sheaf.
mathlib_searches.verdict: no exact Mathlib match; reuse the project API
